title: CSS Cascading Layers (`@layer`) for Specificity Management
topicCategory: 4. Styling Engines & CSS Architecture at Scale
subtopicTitle: CSS Cascading Layers (`@layer`) for Specificity Management
problemStatement:
Eliminating specificity wars and `!important` hacks across design systems and consumer applications using native `@layer`.

**Enterprise Importance**:
CSS Cascade Layers solve the #1 complaint of design system consumers: difficulty overriding component styles without escalating specificity.
interviewTrap: Allowing consumer apps to sprinkle `!important` to override design system styles instead of establishing clear Cascade Layers.

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Layers defined earlier have lower priority than layers defined later, regardless of selector specificity. An element selector in a higher layer beats an ID selector in a lower layer.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Design Token Layer: Primitives, semantic aliases, and component tokens established.
2. Component Architecture: Headless state and keyboard accessibility hooks implemented.
3. Styling & Cascade: Zero-runtime CSS variables and layer specificity managed.
4. Governance & Packaging: Tree-shaking, semantic versioning, and telemetry monitored.

complexity.time: O(1) CSS variable resolution at paint time / zero JavaScript runtime overhead
complexity.space: O(1) bundle footprint per imported component
